does it read there's probably going to be either a shorter version or a longer version the shorter version would just read There are three that Testify the
spirit the water and the blood and these three agree if that's not what you have then you probably have the longer version there are three that testify in
heaven the Father the word and the Holy Spirit these three are one and their three that testify in Earth the spirit
the water and the blood and these three agree that longer version is known as the johannine comma and this is probably the most famous textual variant in all
the Bible it is not in any Greek manuscript of the first epical of John prior to the 13th century CE the
earliest reference of any kind to that longer version of that text as coming from the first Epistle of John is a 4th
Century Latin text called the Libra apologetics that is ostensibly quoting from first John and then in the fifth and sixth centuries we see more Latin
texts quoting the first Epistle of John and attributing that reading to CH 5: 7 and 8 it's very clearly not original
when the Dutch humanist scholar desiderius arasmus published his edition of the Greek New Testament that we now refer to as the texus receptus he did
not include the longer reading the johanan comma because he could tell it was not in any the Greek manuscripts that he was using he got pressure to
include it in later editions and he said he would not include it unless someone could produce a Greek manuscript that was trustworthy that had that reading lo
and behold one suddenly appeared and so reluctantly arasmus included the johannine comma in the Third Edition of
his texus receptus and guess which translation of the Bible into English made use of the Third Edition of arasmus
texus receptus if you guess the King James version you are correct now the King James version became the most famous the most influential English
translation of the Bible of all time and most editions of the King James version include it to this day and we know for a
fact that it was not a part of the first Epistle of John
